items.title: The Supramundane Path Opens: Seven Engagements, Sixteen Aspects, Four Fruits

items.zh: 如是已辯往世間道。若樂往趣出世間道，應當依止四聖諦境，漸次生起七種作意。所謂最初了相作意，最後加行究竟果作意，乃至證得阿羅漢果。
items.en: The mundane path has now been fully explained. If one instead wishes to proceed towards the supramundane path, one should rest on the objects of the four noble truths, giving rise in sequence to seven kinds of mental engagement — from the very first, learning the mark, to the last, the fruit of the culmination of effort — up to the attainment of arhatship itself.

items.zh: 修瑜伽師，於四聖諦略摽、廣辯增上教法，聽聞受持，或於作意已善修習，或得根本靜慮無色。由四種行了苦諦相，謂無常行、苦行、空行、無我行。由四種行了集諦相，謂因行、集行、起行、緣行。由四種行了滅諦相，謂滅行、靜行、妙行、離行。由四種行了道諦相，謂道行、如行、行行、出行。如是名為了相作意。
items.en: A practitioner of yogic discipline, having listened to and upheld the excellent teaching on the four noble truths, both in brief summary and in detailed exposition — whether already well cultivated in the mental engagements, or already having attained the root dhyānas or formless absorptions — comes to know the truth of suffering through four aspects … the truth of origin through four aspects … the truth of cessation through four aspects … and the truth of the path through four aspects. This is called learning the mark.

items.title: The Truth of Suffering's Ten Aspects, Compressed from Four

items.zh: 由十種行觀察苦諦，能隨悟入苦諦四行。何等為十？一、變異行，二、滅壞行，三、別離行，四、法性行，五、合會行，六、結縛行，七、不可愛行，八、不安隱行，九、無所得行，十、不自在行。如是十行，依證成道理能正觀察。
items.en: Through ten aspects one observes the truth of suffering, and is thereby able to enter into its four classical aspects. What are the ten? First, the aspect of change; second, of destruction; third, of separation; fourth, of inherent nature; fifth, of coming-together; sixth, of bondage; seventh, of the undesirable; eighth, of the unsettled; ninth, of nothing to be found; tenth, of powerlessness. One correctly observes by means of these ten aspects, according to the principle of valid proof.

items.title: Section: Impermanence by Scriptural Authority — Beings Die and Are Reborn, Worlds Burn and Vanish

items.zh: 此中且依至教量理。如世尊說：諸行無常。又此諸行略有二種。一、有情世間，二、器世間。世尊依彼有情世間，說如是言：苾芻當知！我以過人清淨天眼，觀諸有情死時、生時，廣說乃至身壞已後，當生善趣天世界中。
items.en: Here, resting first on the principle of scriptural authority: as the World-Honoured One said, all conditioned things are impermanent … these conditioned things, in brief, are of two kinds — the world of sentient beings, and the physical world that contains them … regarding the world of sentient beings, the World-Honoured One spoke thus: monks, you should know that with a pure heavenly eye surpassing that of ordinary humans, I observe beings at the time of their death and at the time of their rebirth — described in full down to the very break-up of the body, after which they are reborn into a fortunate destiny, a heavenly world.

items.zh: 由此法門，顯示世尊以淨天眼，現見一切有情世間是無常性。
又世尊言：苾芻當知！此器世間長時安住，過是已後，漸次乃至七日輪現，如七日經廣說。乃至所有大地、諸山、大海，及蘇迷盧大寶山王，乃至梵世諸器世界，皆被焚燒。災火滅後，灰燼不現，乃至餘影亦不可得。
items.en: And the World-Honoured One further said: monks, you should know that this physical world abides for a very long span of time; but after that span has passed, in due sequence, as many as seven suns come to appear, as the *Discourse on the Seven Suns* explains in full — until every last thing, the great earth, the mountains, the great oceans, even Mount Sumeru itself, the king of great jewelled mountains, up to the entire physical world of the Brahmā realm, is consumed by fire. Once that conflagration has died down, not even ash remains visible, let alone any trace or shadow.

items.zh: 由此法門，世尊顯示諸器世間是無常性。如是且依至教量理，修觀行者淨信增上作意力故，於一切行無常之性獲得決定。得決定已，即由如是淨信增上作意力故，數數尋思觀察一切，現見不背、不由他緣無常之性。云何數數尋思觀察？謂先安立內外二事。言內事者，謂六處等。言外事者，有十六種。一者、地事。謂城邑、聚落、舍、市廛等。二者、園事。謂藥草、叢林等。三者、山事。謂種種山安布差別。四者、水事。謂江、河、陂、湖、眾流、池、沼。五者、作業事。六者、庫藏事。七者、食事。八者、飲事。九者、乘事。十者、衣事。十一者、莊嚴具事。十二者、舞歌樂事。十三者、香鬘塗飾事。十四者、資生具事。十五者、諸光明事。十六者、男女承奉事。如是名為十六種事。安立如是內外事已，復於彼事現見增上作意力故，以變異行尋思觀察無常之性。

items.title: Impermanence by Direct Observation: Fifteen Ordinary Changes in One's Own Body and Mind

items.zh: 此中內事，有十五種所作變異，及有八種變異因緣。云何內事有十五種所作變異？一、分位所作變異，二、顯色所作變異，三、形色所作變異，四、興衰所作變異，五、支節具不具所作變異，六、劬勞所作變異，七、他所損害所作變異，八、寒熱所作變異，九、威儀所作變異，十、觸對所作變異，十一、雜染所作變異，十二、疾病所作變異，十三、終沒所作變異，十四、青瘀等所作變異，十五、一切不現盡滅所作變異。云何八
items.en: As for internal matters, there are fifteen kinds of change brought about … first, change of life-stage; second, of complexion; third, of bodily form; fourth, of rise and decline; fifth, of the limbs being whole or lacking; sixth, of fatigue; seventh, of harm done by others; eighth, of cold and heat; ninth, of posture; tenth, of contact; eleventh, of affliction; twelfth, of illness; thirteenth, of death itself; fourteenth, of the corpse's discoloration; fifteenth, of its final, total disappearance.

One observes, in oneself or in another, that from youth all the way to old age, these continuously arising factors show, from earlier to later, differences unlike one another … thus, by the strengthened power of mental engagement resting on direct observation alone, one observes, through these fifteen aspects, the changing, impermanent nature of one's own internal matters.

blocks.text: Fascicle 34 completes the Śrāvaka Stage. Having described the mundane path, the treatise now describes the **supramundane path**: insight into the four truths, leading through stream-entry to arhatship. It ends with a short account of the fourteenth stage, the **solitary buddha**. A passage (0471a10) is untranslated.

"One should rest on the objects of the four noble truths, giving rise in sequence to seven attentions", from learning the mark to its final fruit, now applied to the truths. One may start from the preparatory concentration or from the root absorptions.

The truth of suffering is observed through ten aspects, which compress into the four classical ones (impermanence, suffering, emptiness, non-self): change, destruction, separation, inherent nature, coming together (these five are impermanence); bondage, the undesirable, the unsettled (suffering); nothing to be found (emptiness); powerlessness (non-self). Master Cháng Bǎi on the last: "one can't have things as one wishes: wanting not to grow old."

The Buddha said all conditioned things are impermanent: both the world of beings ("with a pure divine eye I see beings dying and being reborn") and the physical world, which after a long age is burned by seven suns, "until not even ash remains".

Having gained certainty through scripture and faith, one confirms it by direct observation. One sets out "inner things" (the six sense bases) and sixteen kinds of "outer things": land (towns, houses, markets), gardens, mountains, waters, work, storehouses, food, drink, vehicles, clothes, ornaments, music and dance, perfumes, requisites, lights, and the attentions of men and women. Then one observes how each changes.

Change of life-stage, complexion, form, rise and decline, wholeness of limbs, fatigue, harm by others, heat and cold, posture, contact, defilement, illness, death, the stages of a corpse, and its final disappearance.

quiz.q: "If one wishes to proceed towards the supramundane path, one should rest on" what? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: taking the four noble truths as object, cultivating the seven engagements up to arhatship
quiz.why: "If one instead wishes to proceed towards the supramundane path, one should rest on the objects of the four noble truths, giving rise in sequence to seven kinds of mental engagement." Master Cháng Bǎi: the other road heads for the supramundane path — taking the four noble truths as object, cultivating the seven engagements, attaining the first fruit up to arhatship.

quiz.q: "Whether already well cultivated in the engagements, or having attained the root dhyānas or formless absorptions" — which kinds of yogin? What do the masters think?
options: Cháng Bǎi, after 《披尋記》: the already-practised and the engagement-transcending yogin; Miào Jìng disagrees — beginners and the already-practised
quiz.why: "Whether already well cultivated in the mental engagements, or already having attained the root dhyānas or formless absorptions." Master Cháng Bǎi: having attained root dhyāna or formless absorption should mean the yogin who has transcended the engagements on the mundane path. Venerable Miào Jìng: it should be the beginner and the already-practised yogin — those two.

quiz.q: The first five of the ten aspects lead into which of the four? What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
quiz.why: "What are the ten? First, the aspect of change; second, of destruction; third, of separation; fourth, of inherent nature; fifth, of coming-together …" Master Cháng Bǎi: impermanence has five — one observes it through change, destruction, separation, inherent nature, and coming-together.

quiz.q: The tenth, "powerlessness" — what example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: can't have things as one wishes — wanting not to age won't work
quiz.why: "Tenth, of powerlessness." Master Cháng Bǎi: one can't have things as one wishes — wanting not to grow old doesn't work; one must age.

quiz.q: The ninth, "nothing to be found," leads into which aspect, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
quiz.why: "Ninth, of nothing to be found." Master Cháng Bǎi: emptiness has one aspect — observing the ninth, nothing to be found, one enters emptiness.

quiz.q: "Two kinds: the world of beings and the 器 world." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 器?
options: like fruit set in a vessel
quiz.why: "These conditioned things, in brief, are of two kinds — the world of sentient beings, and the physical world that contains them." Venerable Miào Jìng: like fruit placed in a vessel — that's 器.

quiz.q: "Once the fire dies down, not even ash remains." How does Master Cháng Bǎi view outsiders' doomsday claims?
options: no need to fear — humans have left before the world is destroyed
quiz.why: "Once that conflagration has died down, not even ash remains visible, let alone any trace or shadow." Master Cháng Bǎi: outsiders have all sorts of false doomsday theories; there's no need to fear, because when the world is destroyed, humans have already left it.
